    Compute effect sizes in a recipe

    Source: R/recipes-steps.R
    step_meta_effect_size.Rd

    step_meta_effect_size() creates a specification of a recipe step that computes an effect size and its sampling variance from summary statistics, using the same formulas as meta_effect_size(). The inputs are given as named selections, for example m1 = mean_t, sd1 = sd_t, n1 = n_t, so the names say which role each column plays.

    Usage

    step_meta_effect_size(
  recipe,
  ...,
  measure = "SMD",
  role = "predictor",
  trained = FALSE,
  yi_name = ".yi",
  vi_name = ".vi",
  add = 0.5,
  to = "only0",
  columns = NULL,
  keep_original_cols = TRUE,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("meta_effect_size")
)

# S3 method for class 'step_meta_effect_size'
tidy(x, ...)

    Arguments

    recipe

    A recipe object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this recipe.

    ...

    Named <tidy-select> selections of single columns. The names must be the inputs required by measure (see meta_effect_size()), for example event1, n1, event2 and n2 for "OR".

    measure

    The effect size measure.

    role

    The role of the new columns. Defaults to "predictor"; use recipes::update_role() to make the effect size an outcome.

    trained

    A logical to indicate if the quantities for preprocessing have been estimated.

    yi_name, vi_name

    Names of the new effect size and variance columns.

    add, to

    Zero cell correction, see meta_effect_size().

    columns

    A named character vector of the selected columns. This is NULL until the step is trained by recipes::prep().

    keep_original_cols

    Keep the input columns?

    skip

    A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by recipes::bake()?

    id

    A character string that is unique to this step to identify it.

    x

    A step_meta_effect_size object.

    Value

    An updated version of recipe with the new step added to the sequence of any existing operations. tidy() returns a tibble with columns terms, argument, measure and id.

    See also

    Other recipe steps: step_meta_impute_sd(), step_meta_precision()

    Examples

    library(recipes)
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’:
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’:
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘recipes’
#> The following object is masked from ‘package:stats’:
#> 
#>     step
rec <- recipe(~., data = bcg_trials) |>
  step_mutate(n_t = tpos + tneg, n_c = cpos + cneg) |>
  step_meta_effect_size(event1 = tpos, n1 = n_t, event2 = cpos,
                        n2 = n_c, measure = "RR")
prepped <- prep(rec)
bake(prepped, new_data = NULL)
